desc:
You are given a window [lo, hi) and a list of half-open intervals [start, end), with integer endpoints. The intervals are unsorted, may overlap, and may stick out of the window on either side.

Return the parts of the window that are not covered by any interval, as a sorted list of half-open intervals. Every reported piece must be maximal (two reported pieces never touch) and non-empty. Note that [1, 3) and [3, 5) together leave no hole at 3.

lo = 0, hi = 20
intervals = [[2, 5], [4, 8], [12, 15], [18, 30], [-5, 1]]
result    = [[1, 2], [8, 12], [15, 18]]

If the whole window is covered, return an empty list.
constraints: The window can be huge, so do not walk through it one integer at a time
hints: Computing the complement of a union is easiest when the union is built in order from left to right.
Sort the intervals by start and keep reach, the first point of the window that is not yet known to be covered. Initially reach = lo.
For each interval in order: if end ≤ reach skip it; if start > reach then [reach, min(start, hi)) is a hole; finally set reach = end. After the loop add [reach, hi) if reach < hi.
editorial: Sweep the sorted intervals while keeping reach, the left-most point of the window that is still unexplained. An interval entirely to the left of reach changes nothing. An interval that starts beyond reach proves that [reach, start) is uncovered, because every earlier interval (in sorted order) ends at or before reach and every later one starts even further right. After that, reach jumps to the interval's end.

Clip at the window: stop as soon as reach ≥ hi, and clip a hole's right end to hi. Intervals ending before lo are skipped by the same end ≤ reach rule, since reach starts at lo. Half-open ends make touching intervals leave no hole, and the reported holes are maximal automatically. O(n log n) time for the sort, O(1) extra space besides the result.
